sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy remains the undisputed market leader, while a defensive rotation lifts Healthcare and Real Estate as Utilities and Communication Services falter.

On July 21, 2026, market breadth remains highly concentrated, with only 3 of 11 sectors maintaining "all-green" status across all time horizons. Energy (0.95 momentum) continues to anchor the leadership pack alongside Real Estate (0.67 momentum) and Healthcare (0.63 momentum). 

Pockets of positive rotation are emerging in Consumer Defensive (+1 spot to rank 6) and Financials (+1 spot to rank 7), while Utilities (-2 spots to rank 8) and Communication Services (-1 spot to rank 10) are fading rapidly. Consumer Cyclical remains the deepest laggard with a momentum score of just 0.17.

## Strength
- **Concentrated Breadth:** Only 3 of 11 sectors—Energy, Real Estate, and Healthcare—are "all-green," showing positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD.
- **Energy Dominance:** Energy is the strongest overall sector, holding the #1 YTD rank with a near-perfect momentum score of 0.95.
- **Defensive Strength:** Healthcare (momentum 0.63) and Real Estate (momentum 0.67) solidify their leadership as all-green sectors.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Upward Rotations:** Consumer Defensive (momentum 0.42, rank 6), Financials (momentum 0.62, rank 7), and Healthcare (momentum 0.63, rank 9) each gained +1 spot over the last 5 sessions.
- **Sharp Decliners:** Utilities fell -2 spots to rank 8 with 0.37 momentum, while Communication Services slipped -1 spot to rank 10 with 0.32 momentum.
- **Momentum Extremes:** Technology holds strong at 0.72 momentum (rank 2), while Consumer Cyclical languishes at the bottom with a momentum score of 0.17 (rank 11).

## Divergences
- **Healthcare's Latent Strength:** Healthcare is in the elite "all-green" category and has strong momentum (0.63), yet its YTD rank is low at 9, indicating a powerful, underappreciated turnaround.
- **Industrials Fatigue:** Industrials sits at a high YTD rank of 3, but its momentum has decayed to a lagging 0.35, suggesting the sector is losing steam.
- **No Fragile Leaders:** No fragile all-green sector divergences were flagged in today's data.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Market breadth remains concentrated with 30 of 144 industry groups in "all-green" territory, led by dominant energy and healthcare real estate sectors, while education and metals face sharp weekly declines.

The US industry landscape on July 21, 2026, shows a solid core of leadership, with 30 of 144 groups holding "all-green" status across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD timeframes. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.985) and REIT - Healthcare Facilities (momentum 0.904) anchor this strength. Meanwhile, a rotation is underway as consumer-facing and corporate service niches like Department Stores (+22 spots) and Staffing & Employment Services (+16 spots) surge. 

Underneath the surface, early-warning divergences are appearing. High-momentum groups like Food Distribution and Oil & Gas Midstream are starting to slip in rank, while low-momentum laggards such as Shell Companies and Beverages - Wineries & Distilleries are beginning to jump in rank, signaling a potential shift in capital allocation. Conversely, Education & Training Services (-27 spots) and Aluminum (-21 spots) are experiencing severe momentum breakdowns.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** 30 of 144 groups are positive across all timeframes, led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.98), REIT - Healthcare Facilities (momentum 0.90), and Consumer Electronics (momentum 0.89).
* **Sustained Leadership:** Groups maintaining top-36 status across 1-, 3-, and 6-month ranks include Trucking, Staffing & Employment Services, Healthcare Plans, Textile Manufacturing, and Farm Products.
* **Top Momentum:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing leads overall momentum at 0.985 (YTD rank 3), followed by REIT - Healthcare Facilities at 0.904 (YTD rank 24) and Consumer Electronics at 0.888 (YTD rank 39).

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Shell Companies (+23 spots, rank 73, momentum 0.40), Department Stores (+22 spots, rank 94, momentum 0.66), and Conglomerates (+16 spots, rank 62, momentum 0.60).
* **Top Losers:** Education & Training Services (-27 spots, rank 98, momentum 0.26), Aluminum (-21 spots, rank 85, momentum 0.27), and Aerospace & Defense (-15 spots, rank 104, momentum 0.16).
* **Momentum Laggards:** Bottom-tier momentum is concentrated in Airports & Air Services (momentum 0.082, YTD rank 138) and Mortgage Finance (momentum 0.097, YTD rank 142).

## Divergences
* **Fading Momentum:** High-momentum groups slipping in rank over the last 5 sessions include Food Distribution (momentum 0.61, rank -9), Oil & Gas Midstream (momentum 0.72, rank -5), and Railroads (momentum 0.81, rank -3).
* **Emerging Rank:** Low-momentum groups showing sudden rank improvements include Shell Companies (+23 spots, momentum 0.40), Beverages - Wineries & Distilleries (+12 spots, momentum 0.45), and Packaged Foods (+12 spots, momentum 0.50).
